subject: Human Body
title: Why Fiber Matters
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why Fiber Matters.

hook.text: Humans can't digest fiber. Yet doctors say it's essential. Why eat something you can't break down?

buildup.text: Fiber adds bulk to stool and keeps it soft, preventing constipation. It also speeds transit through the colon.

discovery.text: Soluble fiber feeds gut bacteria, which produce short-chain fatty acids. These nourish colon cells directly.

twist.text: Low-fiber diets are linked to colorectal cancer, diabetes, and heart disease. The connection is dose-dependent.

climax.text: Fiber is food for your gut bacteria, bulk for your stool, and protection for your colon. All in one.

punchline.text: You can't digest fiber. Your gut bacteria can — and they thank you.

quiz.question: Why is fiber important even though humans can't digest it?
options: It provides calories when converted by the liver
It feeds gut bacteria and adds bulk to stool
